bandReport.notes:
All four assigned pages opened and read from the column crops (c1 then c2); no page was empty. Page indices map to printed pages 27, 29, 31, 33.

PASSAGES. Item 53 is governed by 'Passage—3' of a directions block that opens on page 24 (band b3's territory). I opened p24-c2 to check the boundary: it shows 'Passage—2' governing item 52 and the printed page 25 footer, so in that block each passage governs exactly ONE item and Passage—3 begins cleanly at the top of my page 26 with nothing carried over. I did not transcribe items 51/52.
Items 61, 62 and 63 belong to a NEW block that opens on my page 30: 'Directions for the following 3 (three) items : Read the following three passages and answer the items that follow the passages. Your answers to these items should be based on the passages only.' Again one passage per item — Passage—1 -> 61, Passage—2 -> 62, Passage—3 -> 63. Each passage is in its own item's `context` only; the Directions preamble is not in any `context`.
Passage—2 (item 62) SPANS THE GUTTER on page 30: it begins in c1 and continues in c2 ('...seek to overcome “thin' / 'profit margins by gathering...'). Passage—3 (item 63) SPANS THE PAGE BREAK: it begins at the foot of page 30 c2 and finishes at the top of page 32 c1 ('...an economic dead' / 'end or a world in which...'). Both were stitched from the column crops in c1-then-c2 order.

TERRITORY I DO NOT OWN. Page 24 (b3): printed page 25, ends with item 52 complete — nothing of mine starts there. Page 34 (b5): printed page 35, opens cleanly with item 66 (a fresh data-sufficiency item), so item 65 is whole on my page 32 and there is no straddle at either end of my band.

CROP QUALITY. p30-c2 and p24-c2 are SLICED: both carry a narrow strip of the PREVIOUS column's right-hand line endings down their left edge (p30 gutterX=781, p24 gutterX=796, against ~810-827 elsewhere). Those fragments are duplicated remnants, not missing text — I verified against p30-c1, which retains every line ending in full, and the c1->c2 sentence continuations join perfectly. p30-c1 does clip the printed page number at bottom right ('3' for '31'); no body text is affected. No content was read from the whole-page images.

DATA SUFFICIENCY. Items 59, 60, 64, 65 share the same boilerplate opening and the same four options. Per the brief their Question / Statement-I / Statement-II lines are in the STEM, not `context`, so their hashes stay distinct. Item 65 additionally carries a scene-setting line above 'Question :' ('A certain amount was distributed among X, Y and Z.') which is unique to that item and is therefore also in the stem.

PRINTED ODDITIES, transcribed verbatim and NOT corrected:
- Item 60, Statement-II prints the decimal with a raised middle dot: '2·4 kilobytes per second' (kept as U+00B7).
- Item 64 prints its two Statements inline on one line each ('Statement–I : x / y is odd.'), unlike items 59/60/65 which put the statement on its own indented line; Statement-II ('xy = 12') ends with no full stop while Statement-I does.
- Item 63 passage prints 'Resource intensive and, in particular energy intensive processes' — the comma sits after 'and' with none after 'in particular'. Left exactly as printed.
- Item 53 passage prints a comma splice: 'with a unique ability, they can induce the plant...'. Left as printed.
- Item 58 option (d) is broken across two lines with the second line right-indented ('Neither Conclusion–I nor' / 'Conclusion–II follows'); this is line-wrapping only and is transcribed as one sentence.
- Statement/Conclusion labels use an en dash as printed (Statement–I, Conclusion–II).
No duplicated options, no illegible text, no missing item numbers: 53-65 inclusive, each exactly once.

questions.context: Evolution has endowed caterpillars that feed on corn with a unique ability, they can induce the plant to turn off its defence against insect predators. This helps caterpillars to eat more and grow faster. The agent that causes this effect is the caterpillar’s faeces or frass. The find could throw new light on compounds associated with plant response to pathogens like fungi or bacteria.
questions.stem: Which one of the following statements best reflects the most logical, rational and practical message conveyed by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Farmers can use caterpillars to feed on weeds in their crop fields/plantations.

options.label: B
options.text: This finding can help in the development of clinically useful antimicrobial compounds.

options.label: C
options.text: This finding can help in the development of organic, ecologically sustainable pesticides.

options.label: D
options.text: Caterpillars can be genetically modified to be predators of the other plant pests.

A Statement is given followed by two Conclusions numbered I and II. Consider the Statement and the Conclusions.
Statement :
India is the world’s largest producer of milk.
Conclusion–I :
India is the world’s largest exporter of milk.
Conclusion–II :
India does not import milk.
Which one of the following is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Only Conclusion–I follows

options.label: B
options.text: Only Conclusion–II follows

options.label: C
options.text: Both Conclusion–I and Conclusion–II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither Conclusion–I nor Conclusion–II follows

questions.stem:
A Question is given followed by two Statements I and II. Consider the Question and the Statements.
Question :
What are the values of \(m\) and \(n\), where \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers?
Statement–I :
\(m + n > mn\) and \(m > n\).
Statement–II :
The product of \(m\) and \(n\) is 24.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Question and the Statements?

options.label: A
options.text: The Question can be answered by using one of the Statements alone, but cannot be answered using the other Statement alone

options.label: B
options.text: The Question can be answered by using either Statement alone

options.label: C
options.text: The Question can be answered by using both the Statements together, but cannot be answered using either Statement alone

options.label: D
options.text: The Question cannot be answered even by using both the Statements together

questions.context: In a robust democracy, reality, howsoever inconvenient it may be, finds its expression both in the speech of political leaders and the other social forms of assertion. The existence of the real has to be transparent, both through its circulation in and by the media as well as its argumentative articulation in deliberative democracy. A normatively responsible media through its communication effect has the responsibility to circulate the content of reality without distortion.
questions.stem: Which one of the following statements best reflects the crux of the above passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Responsible media should not distort the real in an ideal democracy.

options.label: B
options.text: Fake news seems inherent in the life of an ideal democracy.

options.label: C
options.text: There should not be any kind of restrictions on the freedom of expression in an ideal democracy.

options.label: D
options.text: Irresponsible media and political leaders cannot be effectively controlled in an ideal democracy.

questions.context: Now-a-days there is a growing trend to use interconnected home devices. As consumers increasingly network their homes, the connected home device manufacturers and service providers will seek to overcome “thin profit margins by gathering more of our personal data—with or without our agreement—turning the home into a corporate storefront”. Corporate marketers will have powerful incentives to observe consumer behaviour to understand the buying needs and preferences of the device owners.
questions.stem: Which one of the following statements best reflects the most logical, rational and practical message implied by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Knowledge of consumer behaviour leads to more capital expenditure in manufacturing sector.

options.label: B
options.text: Knowledge of consumer behaviour stimulates the growth of commerce and trade and thus helps in the overall economic development of the country.

options.label: C
options.text: Interconnected devices give a lot of comfort to home users and improve the overall quality of life.

options.label: D
options.text: Interconnected devices can be at security risk and home users may have privacy risk.

questions.context: Green growth involves rethinking growth strategies with regard to the impacts on environmental sustainability and the environmental resources available to poor and vulnerable groups. In rethinking growth, we need to focus on the current reality of a resource-constrained world. Resource intensive and, in particular energy intensive processes will need to make way for more efficient and resource frugal development strategies if we are to avoid an economic dead end or a world in which only a small elite is able to enjoy affluence in the midst of a sea of poverty.
questions.stem: Which one of the following statements best reflects the crux of the above passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Environmental sustainability is inimical to our objective of achieving a high rate of GDP growth.

options.label: B
options.text: Poverty eradication is not possible without a rapid economic growth and the consequent environmental degradation.

options.label: C
options.text: Maintaining high environmental standards is now a prerequisite for achieving a steady, sufficient and inclusive growth.

options.label: D
options.text: With large populations, rampant poverty and limited resources of today’s world, environmental degradation cannot be prevented and inequalities are inevitable.
